title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-scratchpad-2
content:
Context:
- Noted a ~25-40% throughput regression in the dedicated pool serving bert-small-quantized-v2 since 2024-11-04 night deploy. Latency (p50/p95/p99) didn't change drastically for small requests, but aggregate tokens/sec dropped and tail queue length increased.
- Suspected continuous-batching config change from last deploy (PR 812) that adjusted max-batch-size and idle_flush_ms.
- This doc is my scratchpad for commands tried, outputs, quick hypotheses, and next steps.

Immediate hypothesis (top-of-head):
1) Continuous-batching config mismatch: idle_flush_ms increased too much -> longer batching windows for small, low-concurrency requests -> lower tokens/sec (higher per-request latency sometimes).
2) KV cache invalidation: new code path touched cache TTL causing more KV-cache misses -> more compute per request -> lower throughput.
3) Autoscaler oscillation: node churn or pod restart frequency increased resulting in less steady concurrency and cold caches.

Quick metrics observed (from Grafana):
- baseline (2024-11-03): 48k tokens/sec aggregate for pool-bert-1
- post-deploy (2024-11-05): 31k tokens/sec aggregate (≈35% drop)
- concurrent inflight requests: stable at ~120, queue_depth spiked from 8->38 during the incident window
- p99 latency increased from 420ms -> 860ms (but many requests still ~<500ms)
- CPU/GPU utilization: GPU util dropped ~20% despite higher queue depth (suspicious)
- network egress unchanged

Commands/queries I ran (with outputs paraphrased):
1) k get pods -n dedicated-pool --selector=pool=pool-bert-1 -o wide
   -> all pods Running, restarts 0-1, age 3d
2) kubectl logs pod/bert-1-5 -c runtime --since=2h | grep "batching" -n
   -> logs show: "continuous-batcher: set idle_flush_ms=40" and later "batcher: flushed 32 requests, avg_wait_ms=78"
3) git diff origin/main..HEAD -- serving/runtime/continuous_batching_config.go
   -> PR 812 changed default idle_flush_ms from 20 -> 40 and max_batch_size from 64 -> 128 for some pools behind feature flag.
4) curl -s http://localhost:9090/metrics | grep continuous_batcher | head -n 20
   -> continuous_batcher_inflight{pool="pool-bert-1"} 22
      continuous_batcher_avg_wait_ms{pool="pool-bert-1"} 76.2
      continuous_batcher_batch_size_histogram{pool="pool-bert-1"} buckets: most mass at 8-16 (unexpected given max_batch_size 128)
5) rtv request tracing for a sample request (trace id abc123)
   -> saw batching wait 80ms, model_execution 12ms, queuing 4ms, serialization 3ms
   -> many requests have short model_execution time but higher wait_ms -> suggests underfilled batches, so increasing max_batch_size shouldn't reduce throughput, increasing idle_flush_ms might hurt.

Reproduction attempts locally (mini cluster):
- Replayed traffic with same RPS but higher connection churn: throughput similar to pre-deploy when idle_flush_ms=20.
- With idle_flush_ms=40, observed lower tokens/sec when request inter-arrival variance is high (spiky small requests).

Error/strange snippets from runtime logs:
- "warn: batcher flush while no inflight requests (race)" - rare
- "kvcache: miss for key session:... (miss_count++)" - miss rate ~2x higher on post-deploy period (from 0.5% -> 1.2%)
- "scheduler: scheduled 3 tasks, but gpu idle" - seen in 3 pods around 02:14 UTC

Hypotheses refined after logs/metrics:
- Primary: idle_flush_ms increase (20->40ms) makes batching windows double; on workloads with high variance and many small requests, this increases average latency per request and reduces tokens/sec because batches are under-utilized (we saw batch size histogram mass at 8-16 not near max). The longer window increases head-of-line waiting and reduces steady throughput due to pacing mismatch.
- Secondary: KV cache miss increase may be correlated with pod restarts (cold caches) or a TTL code change. Need to inspect PR 812 for KV lines. If more compute per request occurs due to misses, that can reduce throughput.
- Tertiary: Autoscaler heuristics (scale down faster) caused temporary GPU idle periods and cold-starts. The "gpu idle" log suggests scheduling mismatch at times.

Quick config audit (PR 812):
- changes: idle_flush_ms default bumped, max_batch_size bumped behind ff, introduced a small refactor touching kv-cache refresh logic (lines in kv_cache_manager.go) - potential bug?
- action: revert idle_flush_ms change for pool-bert-1 as an A/B test (rollout only to pool-bert-1).

Planned short experiments (can run in minutes-hours):
1) A/B rollback: change idle_flush_ms back to 20 for pool-bert-1 on 1 pod (canary) -> measure tokens/sec and p99 over 30m. (Low risk)
2) Force warm KV cache: run a warm-up job that replays top-100 keys to populate cache on all pods. Measure miss_rate. (Low risk)
3) Temporarily pin max_batch_size=64 to verify batch shape effects.
4) Increase autoscaler stabilization window (if scale events correlate) and see if GPU idle logs stop.

Commands to execute experiment 1 (A/B rollback):
- kubectl -n dedicated-pool set env deployment/bert-1 BATCHER_IDLE_FLUSH_MS=20 --record
- watch curl -s https://grafana.redwood.ai/api/datasources/proxy/1/api/v1/query?query=rate(tokens_processed_total[1m])  (manual polling)
- kubectl logs -f deployment/bert-1 -c runtime | grep "continuous-batcher"

Notes/timestamps (for incident breadcrumbs):
- 2024-11-04 23:12 UTC: deploy merged (PR 812)
- 2024-11-05 00:30 UTC: initial alert triggered (tokens/sec drop)
- 2024-11-05 00:45 UTC: first triage, noticed idle_flush_ms change in diff
- 2024-11-05 01:10 UTC: rolled canary revert on 1 pod (temporary) -> tokens/sec bounced ~10% on that pod but aggregate still low (probably need full pool revert)
- 2024-11-05 03:00 UTC: warmed caches, miss rate returned to baseline, small improvement in throughput (~6%)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is the idle_flush_ms change safe for high-throughput, low-variance workloads? (probably yes) For high-variance workloads it's harmful. Need feature-flag per-pool defaults.
- Is there a bug in KV cache refactor? Need code review on kv_cache_manager.go lines touched in PR 812 (ask Marco).
- Autoscaler: correlate kube events and HPA/VM scale times across the time window (ask SRE to pull events).

Immediate next actions (today):
- [ ] Run full-pool revert of idle_flush_ms to 20 for pool-bert-1 and monitor 1 hour (talk to release-engineering for safe rollout)
- [ ] Run warmup job across pods to ensure caches warm (script in infra tooling: tools/warm_kv_cache.sh)
- [ ] Add more granular batch_size histogram logging (per-request sampling) to see real distribution under production.
- [ ] Create follow-up JIRA: INF-3250 "Investigate kv-cache TTL/behavior after PR 812" and link this doc / logs.

Notes to self about communications:
- Keep incident notes concise for customer update: cause = batching window increase + cache warmup + autoscaler chirps. Risk: not fully proven until KV cache code review.
- Slack update template: short summary + what we changed + what we're monitoring + expected rollback window.

Random scratch ideas to test later:
- Try adaptive idle_flush_ms based on recent inter-arrival statistics (micro-optimizer)
- Expose per-model workload profiles so default continuous-batching params are tuned per-model (e.g., chat vs. completion)

End of scratchpad. Will iterate as I run the A/B revert and gather fine-grained traces.

Changelist for doc: 2024-11-05 initial notes -> 2024-11-06 added logs/traces -> 2024-11-14 final hypotheses and action items (still draft)
